theorems_and_formulations.name: Constrained Multi-Objective Optimization Problem
theorems_and_formulations.equation: min_pi E[(1-r)E_1 + r(E_1+E_2)] s.t. E[(1-r)L_1 + r(L_1+L_2)] <= L_SLA, E[R_task] <= epsilon_risk
theorems_and_formulations.verification_notes: The decision variable pi(x) = P(r=1|x) lies in the convex functional space Pi: X -> [0, 1]. The objective functional is affine in pi. The latency constraint is affine in pi. The risk functional is convex in pi under the assumption that invoking a stronger model weakly decreases expected task error. Thus, the optimization problem is a convex functional program.

theorems_and_formulations.name: Theorem 1: Zero Duality Gap in Continuum Edge Cascades
theorems_and_formulations.statement: min_pi max_lambda,mu L(pi, lambda, mu) = max_lambda,mu min_pi L(pi, lambda, mu)
assumptions_required: Policy space Pi is the convex set of measurable functions X -> [0, 1].
Expected task risk functional E[R_task(pi)] is convex in pi.
Slater's condition holds: there exists an interior policy pi_0 in Pi such that E[L(pi_0)] < L_SLA and E[R_task(pi_0)] < epsilon_risk.
theorems_and_formulations.slater_condition_analysis: Strict feasibility is satisfied when the all-heavy policy pi(x)=1 satisfies the risk constraint strictly, while queueing admission control or appropriate baseline latency guarantees average latency feasibility for randomized combinations.

theorems_and_formulations.name: Pollaczek-Khinchine M/G/1 Queueing Analysis
theorems_and_formulations.equation: W_q = lambda E[S^2] / (2(1 - rho)), rho = lambda E[S] < 1
assumptions_required: Frame inter-arrival times are independent and exponentially distributed (M) or periodic.
Service times are general i.i.d. random variables with finite second moment E[S^2].
Stability condition rho = lambda E[S] < 1 is strictly satisfied.
theorems_and_formulations.arrival_model_qualification: Camera video frames arrive periodically with C_a^2 -> 0. The M/G/1 Poisson arrival assumption (C_a^2 = 1) serves as a rigorous upper bound on buffer delay (G/G/1 mean waiting time is bounded above by M/G/1 under Kingman's bound).

theorems_and_formulations.name: Kingman Heavy-Traffic Approximation & Tail Delay
theorems_and_formulations.equation: P(W_q > t) approx exp(- 2(1 - rho) t / (lambda Var(S)/E[S] + E[S]))
theorems_and_formulations.qualification: Kingman's approximation provides an asymptotic upper bound on the tail delay distribution as rho -> 1 for general G/G/1 queues.

theorems_and_formulations.name: Energy-Delay Product (EDP) Metric
theorems_and_formulations.equation: EDP = E[E] * E[L] = (E_1 + r_bar E_2) * (L_1 + r_bar L_2)
theorems_and_formulations.derivation_note: d(EDP)/d(r_bar) = E_2(L_1 + r_bar L_2) + L_2(E_1 + r_bar E_2) = E_2 L_1 + E_1 L_2 + 2 r_bar E_2 L_2 > 0, showing that EDP is strictly monotonically increasing in heavy model invocation rate r_bar. Minimizing EDP under task risk constraints pushes the policy to the boundary of the risk constraint.
